repository.description: Canonical repository identity for custody and retrieval; one repository may contain several independently identified resources.

entrypoint.description: Path identifying this resource definition within its repository. A branch or tag selects a revision without creating another host identity.

sources.description: Named source documents containing proposed configuration. A repository may hold several host or app entrypoints; publication does not admit or activate them.

source.description: Source definition for this named host, identified by canonical repository and entrypoint rather than a repository alias or mutable ref.

operating_mode.description: Intended operating pattern for this host. Observations report current reachability and power separately; a missed response does not change this expectation.

source.description: Source definition for this application, separate from its admitted release, running components, and durable data.

host.description: Declared placement for the application. Editing this selection proposes a move; admission and activation require separately authorized owner work.

placement_generation.description: Expected placement generation used to detect stale placement decisions. Editing source does not advance an owner's accepted generation.

boundary_digest.description: Digest of the exact declared application boundary to be reviewed and checked during admission.

Domain.description: An independently administered collection of hosts and applications. Domain identity is separate from DNS naming, Git custody, and the permissions enforced by each receiving owner.

concerns.description: Concern and binding names label declarations; they do not partition native targets. Services and packages explicitly select receiving-owner-enrolled adapters and exact grant scopes. Provider-owned pinned source schemas define native selectors, including service units, labels and package names. Before planning or dispatch, the receiver resolves each declaration through an independently approved SourceTargetBinding and rejects duplicate canonical native mutation targets across concerns, selectors and instances, even when prescriptions agree. Declaration order grants no precedence. Notifications name exactly one validated service binding and use that same accepted target; they cannot select another executor. Ordinary files, secret files and artifacts share one absolute destination namespace. Destination paths use canonical absolute spelling without empty, dot or parent segments or a trailing slash. Lexical source checks cannot establish native separation; native admission must resolve aliases, confine all side effects and reject overlapping writers.

adapter.description: Explicit selection of an already receiving-owner-enrolled software instance. Native target syntax belongs to its pinned source schema; source cannot enroll or reconfigure that instance.

scope.description: Exact accepted software grant scope. Planning and notifications resolve this selector through the independently approved SourceTargetBinding; no platform default or inferred executor is permitted.

additionalProperties.description: Desired state for one native target selected through an exact owner-approved adapter and canonical namespace mapping. The source selector identifies the native target; desired changes do not create a different target. Native capability and current mutation permission are checked separately before execution.

adapter.description: Explicit selection of an already receiving-owner-enrolled service instance. Native target syntax belongs to its pinned source schema; source cannot enroll or reconfigure that instance.

scope.description: Exact accepted service grant scope. Planning and notifications resolve this selector through the independently approved SourceTargetBinding; no platform default or inferred executor is permitted.

additionalProperties.description: Desired state for one native target selected through an exact owner-approved adapter and canonical namespace mapping. The source selector identifies the native target; desired changes do not create a different target. Native capability and current mutation permission are checked separately before execution.

runtime_instance.description: Host-approved runtime assignment for this application account. New runtime work requires the application's requested runtime instance and the receiving owner's accepted runtime binding to name this same enrolled instance. This is an admission constraint, not a default that application source can override. Changing source alone neither rebinds accepted work nor alters its recovery authority.

Host.description: A source definition for one computer and its managed configuration. Its named identity is independent of its source repository and current address or reachability; accepted work remains with its local owner.

runtime.description: Application-requested runtime selection. Admission joins this request to the host-approved account assignment and the receiving owner's accepted binding, including the enrolled installation and configuration. This request cannot enroll an instance, override the host assignment or implicitly rebind accepted work.

readiness_hook.description: Names a health hook with read mode. Readiness is observational and cannot invoke restore, configure, transition or other write procedures. The hook retains its declared executor and exact data/secret/network grants; referencing it here never broadens them.

custody.description: Who is responsible for recovery of this dataset: this application, or the explicitly named external owner.

recovery.description: Declared recovery policy, separate from custody and storage lifetime. Preserve requires capture and restore; rebuild requires reconstruction and verification; external delegates recovery to the named owner. A declaration is neither recovery proof nor permission to delete data.

verify_restore.description: Read-only verification hook for restoring a preserved dataset.

owner.description: Resource responsible for a referenced dataset. Datasets managed by this application use null because the enclosing application owns their recovery.

rebuild.description: Declared write hook that reconstructs a dataset for which this app is responsible from retained inputs. Invoking it requires separately authorized owner work.

verify_rebuild.description: Read-only hook that verifies reconstructed data before it is accepted as usable.

additionalProperties.description: Hook roles determine their access mode. Observation, assessment, verification and capture use read access to admitted datasets; configure, quiesce, transition application, restore and rebuild use write access and require separately authorized owner work. Read access also constrains remote credentials and native operations: a read-only filesystem mount alone does not make a database connection observational. Artifact output is confined separately to the operation output directory. Restore and verify-restore invocations carry the selected checkpoint, exact dataset snapshots and read-only artifact materializations through hook-request.restore_input, separately from dataset targets. The receiving owner verifies that handoff against retained accepted inputs; procedure names and release identity cannot select a capture implicitly.

secret_bindings.description: Each component and canonical absolute target pair has one secret-delivery declaration, regardless of binding name, secret entry or delivery mode. Different component namespaces may use the same target spelling. Native admission must verify that their actual destinations remain independently scoped.

maintenance.description: Proposed task definitions, not grants of authority. The receiver resolves the exact task from its accepted release and requires at least both app.maintenance-run's minimum role and the expanded action's minimum role, within the current resource scope. Built-in backup, backup-check and drill tasks have no hook override. Native-maintenance selects one declared hook and requires administrator regardless of its hook role, while retaining its exact approved hook scope and all role-specific input and custody requirements. This rule applies to manual and scheduled execution. A schedule, task name or source change cannot delegate administrator authority.

calendar.description: systemd OnCalendar expression under the pinned native calendar parser selected by calendar_language; an unparsed or ambiguous candidate is never admissible. Syntactic validity is necessary but not an execution grant.

timezone.description: IANA time-zone identifier resolved against an admitted pinned timezone database. Missing/ambiguous identifiers reject the task before admission; current host timezone is never an implicit default.

calendar_language.description: The selected v1 calendar dialect. A qualified native owner must parse and normalize this expression using its pinned calendar implementation before admission; unsupported expressions block, never fall back to a different syntax.

dst_policy.description: Nonexistent wall-clock times are skipped. Repeated local wall times execute once using the first occurrence. The identity of the due occurrence persists across reboot, clock changes and retry.

catch_up.description: At most the latest eligible missed due occurrence is attempted after downtime; no storm or independent overlap. Retain due/attempt/result identities across owner restart.

additionalProperties.description: The receiver persists task occurrence identity (accepted release, task, due instant and DST fold), attempt and result, with receiver-local continuing authorization. Revoked permissions stop new attempts and detached client state never governs the schedule.

App.description: A source definition for one independently operated application, including its components, interfaces, and data responsibilities. Placement belongs to the Domain; a source revision, admitted release, running component, and dataset are distinct objects.

repository.description: Identity of the repository that owns this logical catalogue. Admission verifies it against the accepted source closure; it is not the selected provider location.

source.description: Explicit request for an owner-approved secret-source instance and descriptor-validated provider source selector. The receiving owner must check the secret-source role, exact permitted scope, installed artifact, configuration and source-schema identity. Provider locators and credentials belong to that instance or its provider-owned source schema. This declaration cannot install, configure, grant authority to or implicitly rebind an instance. Admitted work retains the selected instance/configuration identity and exact immutable secret generations; changing this selection does not replace them.

RepoSecrets.description: Repository-owned logical secret catalogue, independent of the secret storage provider. Its repository identifies source custody, not a backend or management permission. Entries never contain values. The source selection names an already owner-approved secret-source instance; publication, credential issuance and consumer adoption remain distinct authorized effects.
